threads.body: Moved before `isIndyEnabled` check so that `helperClassStrategy` method wouldn't be ignored. With this  user specified value for `helperClassStrategy` is honored, but the autodetection is disabled for now unless the indy enabled flag is used.

The `HelperClassStrategy.ISOLATED` branch returns `true` before checking `AgentDistributionConfig.get().isIndyEnabled()`, which contradicts the comment that indy "currently needs to be enabled with a flag" and changes prior behavior (a module can force indy even when the global indy flag is off). If the flag is still intended to gate indy, consider only honoring `ISOLATED` after the flag check (while still allowing `INJECTED` to force-disable).

replies.body: No code change at afa2a783213b22a0b10fb09ee081f3bf24902c41: the reordered check is intentional so explicit INJECTED or ISOLATED module strategies are honored, while the global indy flag gates only DEFAULT autodetection; the referenced "currently needs to be enabled with a flag" comment was removed by this PR.

threads.body: [Documentation] Moving this enum removes `ExperimentalInstrumentationModule.HelperClassStrategy` and changes the strategy method's return type for extension authors, making this a breaking change to a non-stable API. `CONTRIBUTING.md:15-25` requires an Unreleased changelog entry and migration notes for such changes; neither is currently present. Please document the old-to-new type and method migration.

[Testing] The strategy lookup now applies to plain `InstrumentationModule` implementations, including the intentional ability for `INJECTED` and `ISOLATED` to override the global indy setting, but no test currently exercises `helperClassStrategy()`. Add cases using a module that does not implement `ExperimentalInstrumentationModule` for all three strategy values with indy enabled and disabled.

[Testing] `AdviceInspectorTest` covers default and advice-annotation detection, but not these newly marker-free hooks. Add plain `InstrumentationModule` cases overriding `injectedClassNames()` and `exposedClassNames()` to verify that each promoted hook selects isolated advice without implementing `ExperimentalInstrumentationModule`.
I didn't find any overrides of this method, is it needed?

replies.body:
Usually we rely on muzzle plugin to decide whether to inject or isolate helper classes. If muzzle is not applied to the plugin we'll do the same detection at runtime. This method can be used to avoid the runtime detection or set the helper class strategy manually. I added this mostly for completeness, muzzle is optional and most of extension functionality (should be everything except virtual fields) is available without it. Since the default behavior is to guess I thought it would be nice to have let users explicitly choose. Our detection fails when instrumentation mixes inline and non-inline advice and falls back to inline though really I guess it could work with isolated helper classes when simple advice is inlined.
That being said I don't feel strongly about it, if you prefer I believe this could be moved back to experimental. I'd expect the defaults to work nicely so quite possible that nobody really needs this.
I ended up removing it back to experimental and improved the javadoc a bit for `injectedClassNames()` and `exposedClassNames()`

threads.body: [General] Removing `injectedClassNames()` and `exposedClassNames()` from this interface is source- and binary-incompatible for extensions that call them through `ExperimentalInstrumentationModule` (previous bytecode uses `invokeinterface` and will fail with `NoSuchMethodError`). Per `CONTRIBUTING.md:15-25`, either retain deprecated default declarations for a compatibility window, or document this as a breaking change with an Unreleased changelog entry and migration notes.

replies.body: No code change: No code change: extensions only implement injectedClassNames() and exposedClassNames(), while agent/tooling calls them through InstrumentationModule. Existing overrides continue to dispatch, and non-overriding implementations retain the same empty-list behavior from the new superclass defaults. Without external invokeinterface callers, removing the experimental interface declarations does not break behavior or linkage.
